quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: When do large trucks lose speed?

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks lose speed going up long or steep hills because they take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. Leave extra space when driving behind a large truck, especially on hills.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the accelerator to slow down gradually. Do not brake until the vehicle has slowed a lot.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: The first half hour of rain is dangerous because water mixes with oil and other chemicals on the road that have not washed away yet. Drive with extra caution on slippery roads.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. When both headlights are visible in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return to your lane.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: For any turn, use the lane closest to the direction you want to turn into. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What problems can sudden wind gusts cause on highways?

options.text: They affect only large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can affect all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong winds can cause problems for all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust into the road and can physically move any vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about hazards ahead. Round signs are only used to warn about railroad crossings.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: You check your blind spots by:

options.text: Looking in your side mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
Looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual events:

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at crashes or unusual events. This causes traffic to back up and creates congestion.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol damages your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol damages your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your judgment. Good judgment is needed to react correctly to things on the road. Any amount of alcohol can hurt your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless you cannot find a safe gap to merge.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use your low beam headlights.
Use your high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near. Switch to low beams when following another driver.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A yellow five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and stop if any are in the crosswalk.

questions.question: As vehicle speed increases, stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease.
Do not change.
Increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must turn and look over your shoulders to see these areas.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop completely before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians, but you do not need to stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than passenger cars.
They all have air brakes that let them stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much more distance to stop. A car going 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A truck at the same speed needs about 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medicines and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe if you take the right dose.
All prescription medicines are safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines often cause drowsiness. You must know how your medicine affects you before driving.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Always use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Never change lanes suddenly or without looking.
